steps.name: environment
steps.description: Prepare workspace and workspace-scoped environment for headless frontend development. Validates node >=16 and npm presence. Writes a workspace-local env file at WORKSPACE/.env.local containing NODE_ENV=development and CI=true by default. If WORKSPACE/.enable_global_env exists, writes /etc/profile.d/webfrontend_env.sh atomically (backups existing) to persist NODE_ENV and CI and prepend npm global bin to PATH.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-finding-app-98606-98491/WebFrontend"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "error: node not found" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v npm >/dev/null || { echo "error: npm not found" >&2; exit 3; }
NODE_V=$(node -v)
NODE_MAJOR=$(node -p "parseInt(process.version.replace(/^v/,'').split('.')[0]) || 0")
if [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -lt 16 ]; then echo "error: Node >=16 required, found ${NODE_V}" >&2; exit 4; fi
NPM_V=$(npm -v || echo "0")
NPM_MAJOR=$(echo "$NPM_V" | cut -d. -f1 || echo "0")
if [ -z "$NPM_MAJOR" ] || [ "$NPM_MAJOR" -lt 7 ]; then echo "warning: npm >=7 recommended, found ${NPM_V}" >&2; fi
if [ -f "$WORKSPACE/.enable_global_env" ]; then
  NPM_PREFIX=$(npm config get prefix 2>/dev/null || echo "/usr/local")
  NPM_BIN="$NPM_PREFIX/bin"
  SVC_FILE="/etc/profile.d/webfrontend_env.sh"
  [ -f "$SVC_FILE" ] && sudo cp "$SVC_FILE" "${SVC_FILE}.bak.$(date +%s)"
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  sudo tee "$tmp" >/dev/null <<EOF
# WebFrontend global environment (development only)
export NODE_ENV=development
export CI=true
case ":\$PATH:" in
  *":${NPM_BIN}:") :;;
  *) export PATH="${NPM_BIN}:\$PATH";;
esac
EOF
  sudo mv "$tmp" "$SVC_FILE" && sudo chmod 644 "$SVC_FILE"
  echo "wrote $SVC_FILE"
else
  ENVF="$WORKSPACE/.env.local"
  cat > "$ENVF" <<EOF
# WebFrontend workspace-local env
NODE_ENV=development
CI=true
EOF
  chmod 644 "$ENVF"
  echo "wrote $ENVF"
fi
echo "node:${NODE_V} npm:${NPM_V}"

steps.name: testing
steps.description: Ensure tests can run in the workspace. If package.json exists, back it up before modification. If package.json is missing and the workspace is empty or WORKSPACE/.allow_inplace_scaffold exists, create a minimal deterministic package.json, minimal src files, and install vitest dev dependencies locally; otherwise fail fast to avoid accidental overwrite. Create a dummy vitest test (TS if WORKSPACE/USE_TYPESCRIPT present) and run tests with local vitest or fallback to global jest. Leave package.json.bak when package.json was present.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-finding-app-98606-98491/WebFrontend"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
TS_FLAG=0
[ -f "$WORKSPACE/USE_TYPESCRIPT" ] && TS_FLAG=1
# If package.json missing, allow scaffold-only when workspace empty or explicitly allowed
if [ ! -f package.json ]; then
  if [ "$(ls -A . | wc -l)" -gt 0 ] && [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/.allow_inplace_scaffold" ]; then
    echo "error: package.json missing and workspace non-empty. To allow automated minimal scaffold create $WORKSPACE/.allow_inplace_scaffold" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  # create minimal package.json
  cat > package.json <<JSON
{
  "name":"webfrontend-minimal",
  "version":"0.0.0",
  "private":true,
  "scripts":{"test":"vitest","start":"vite","build":"vite build"}
}
JSON
  mkdir -p src/__tests__ src
  if [ "$TS_FLAG" -eq 1 ]; then
    cat > src/main.tsx <<'TS'
import React from 'react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
const App=()=>React.createElement('div',null,'Hello')
const root=document.getElementById('root')
if(root) createRoot(root).render(React.createElement(App))
TS
  else
    cat > src/main.jsx <<'JS'
import React from 'react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
const App=()=>React.createElement('div',null,'Hello')
const root=document.getElementById('root')
if(root) createRoot(root).render(React.createElement(App))
JS
  fi
  npm i --no-audit --no-fund -D vitest jsdom @testing-library/react >/dev/null
fi
# Backup existing package.json if present
[ -f package.json ] && cp package.json package.json.bak || true
# Ensure vitest exists locally and write test
if [ -f node_modules/.bin/vitest ]; then
  mkdir -p src/__tests__
  if [ "$TS_FLAG" -eq 1 ]; then
    cat > src/__tests__/sample.test.ts <<'TS'
import { test, expect } from 'vitest'
test('sanity', ()=>{ expect(true).toBe(true) })
TS
  else
    cat > src/__tests__/sample.test.js <<'JS'
import { test, expect } from 'vitest'
test('sanity', ()=>{ expect(true).toBe(true) })
JS
  fi
  ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run || { echo 'vitest failed' >&2; exit 3; }
  exit 0
fi
# Fallback to global jest
if command -v jest >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mkdir -p src/__tests__
  cat > src/__tests__/sample.jest.js <<'JS'
test('sanity', ()=>{ expect(true).toBe(true) })
JS
  jest --runInBand || { echo 'jest failed' >&2; exit 4; }
  exit 0
fi
echo 'error: no test runner available' >&2; exit 5

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Build the application and perform a smoke test: run npm run build, then serve the build (serve if available) or start the dev server. Start servers under setsid, capture logs in a temp directory, poll the expected port(s) for up to 60s (override with WEB_FRONTEND_PORT), then stop the process group cleanly. On failure surface logs and exit non-zero.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-finding-app-98606-98491/WebFrontend"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
LOG_DIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/webfrontend-logs.XXXX)
BUILD_LOG="$LOG_DIR/build.log"
npm run build >"$BUILD_LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "build failed, see $BUILD_LOG" >&2; tail -n 200 "$BUILD_LOG" >&2 || true; exit 2; }
PORT=${WEB_FRONTEND_PORT:-}
if [ -z "$PORT" ]; then CAND_PORTS=(5000 5173 3000); else CAND_PORTS=("$PORT"); fi
SERVE_CMD=""
if [ -f node_modules/serve/bin/serve.js ]; then SERVE_CMD="node node_modules/serve/bin/serve.js -s build -l"; elif [ -x node_modules/.bin/serve ]; then SERVE_CMD="node node_modules/.bin/serve -s build -l"; fi
if [ -n "$SERVE_CMD" ]; then P=${PORT:-5000}; setsid sh -c "$SERVE_CMD $P" >"$LOG_DIR/serve.out" 2>"$LOG_DIR/serve.err" & PID=$!; sleep 0.3; else setsid npm run start >"$LOG_DIR/dev.out" 2>"$LOG_DIR/dev.err" & PID=$!; sleep 0.8; fi
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$PID" | tr -d ' ' || true)
UP=1
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  for p in "${CAND_PORTS[@]}"; do
    [ -z "$p" ] && continue
    if curl -sSf "http://127.0.0.1:${p}/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then UP=0; break 2; fi
  done
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$UP" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "validation failed: server did not respond" >&2; echo "logs: $LOG_DIR" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG_DIR"/* 2>/dev/null || true
  [ -n "$PGID" ] && kill -- -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
  [ -n "$PID" ] && kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  exit 3
fi
echo "validation ok; server responded. logs: $LOG_DIR"
[ -n "$PGID" ] && kill -- -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
[ -n "$PID" ] && kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true

I kept the scripts idempotent, concise, non-interactive, and using /etc/profile.d only when explicitly enabled by the workspace toggle. Validation still depends on all prior steps. This approach addresses the CRITICAL blocking issue by adding safe, deterministic behavior to the testing step instead of changing the workspace path or requiring manual intervention.

change_logs.message: Refined from initial plan: modified env-01 to safely create /etc/profile.d/webfrontend_env.sh without expanding the invoker's PATH and added permission/validation and node/npm version checks; changed scaffold-01 to use installed create-react-app binary (no npx) and added a deterministic Vite fallback, plus detection of scaffold type and correct package.json script wiring (removed forced react-scripts); corrected deps-01 script_name to 'install', added idempotent dependency checks and use of npm ci when lockfile exists; updated test-01 to install/configure vitest as devDependency when selected and to expose test output and fail on test failures; hardened validation-01 to fail on build errors, prefer local serve binary, implement port polling with timeout and clean process-group termination, and avoid npx downloads during validation. Addressed analyst issues around error swallowing, idempotency, and race conditions.

Refined steps env-01, scaffold-01, deps-01, test-01, and validation-01 to address analyst feedback: fixed here-doc quoting in env-01 to avoid runtime expansion and removed runtime npm calls during write; ensured scaffolding doesn't run CRA into non-empty workspace, replaced malformed index.html generation with deterministic path selection, added tsconfig.json and vite.config.js for TypeScript Vite fallback and removed non-null assertion usage; corrected inverted node -e logic and removed error-suppressing '|| true' in deps-01, aligned 'serve' detection with validation expectations; updated test-01 to set package.json test script deterministically and prefer local runner or global jest executable (no npx); improved validation-01 to launch servers with setsid, capture logs, poll longer, and kill process groups without sudo. These changes resolve correctness, robustness, and policy issues raised by the analyst.

Refined env-01, scaffold-01, deps-01, test-01, and validation-01 to address analyst feedback: env-01 now avoids running npm at shell startup, writes /etc/profile.d/webfrontend_env.sh atomically with backup and a workspace-local toggle (.local_env) and validates existing content; scaffold-01 fixes index entry path, handles non-empty non-React directories deterministically (fails fast or performs in-place Vite scaffold), pins minimal compatible dependency versions and ensures package-lock.json is produced; deps-01 removes silent '|| true' behavior and always produces/retains lockfile, surfaces failures; test-01 preserves existing test script by backing up package.json before modification and writes TS tests when USE_TYPESCRIPT is present and configures vitest TS support; validation-01 consistently uses setsid for all server starts, invokes serve through node wrapper if necessary, exposes configurable PORT via WEB_FRONTEND_PORT, polls appropriate endpoints and inspects build output on failure, and ensures robust process-group cleanup. These changes address CRITICAL and HIGH issues (no runtime npm in profile, reproducible lockfiles, deterministic scaffolding for non-empty dirs, loud installs, TS-aware tests, consistent server lifecycle).

Modified step test-01 to handle missing package.json: if the workspace is empty or WORKSPACE/.allow_inplace_scaffold exists, the test step will create a minimal deterministic package.json, install minimal test dependencies (vitest + jsdom) locally, create a dummy test, run tests, and leave package.json.bak if an original existed. If workspace is non-empty and not allowed, the step still fails fast with a clear message. This change addresses the engineer's blocking report that testing failed due to missing package.json and avoids requiring manual provision of package.json for empty workspaces.
